lines.text: # The Species Classes defined here are the ones you can choose from in the character creator. The portraits for prescripted races are grabbed straight from the .gfx file.
# There is also portrait_sets database that contains sets of portraits associated with species classes.
# 'graphical_culture' is connected to the looks used for ships and cities; see "common/graphical_culture/".
# playable = yes/no/trigger (default: yes)		if this species class can is playable
# randomized = yes/no/trigger (default: yes)	if this species class is randomized
# species_trait_points							base number of species trait points available for this species class
# species_max_traits							maximum number of traits that species of this class can have (doesn't count those with cost == 0)
# gender = yes/no (default: yes)				whether the species has a gender
# portrait_modding yes/no (default: yes)		whether the portrait can be modified with e.g. genemodding or robomodding
# random_weight									increases/reduces the chance of spawning this species class
# ethics_to_prefer								list of ethics certain species class will preffer over others
# preferred_ethics_weight						increases/reduces the chance of this species class choosing one of the preferred ethics
tags = { organic positive habitability leader army lithoid special }
name = civic_wilderness_ascetic # in order to show a new flavor description
# This file is used to provide some customization options for empires.
# for each country, the various customizations are weighted, and the one that ends up with the highest weight is used
default = {										# "default" should always exists as it's the value the engine will always fall back on
base = 1								# a value of 0 will be ignored entirely, otherwise the customization with the highest value wins.
biogenesis_01 = { modifier = { add = 10 graphical_culture = biogenesis_01 } } # Make sure we don't switch
biogenesis_02 = { modifier = { add = 10 graphical_culture = biogenesis_02 } } # Make sure we don't switch
# Rules to define the behavior of gui elements
#Check if planets resources should be hidden
priority = 0					#priority decides in which order the scenarios are listed
radius = 200					#should be less than 500, preferably less than ~460

findings.result: lith11 is a native LITHOID portrait used in an official preset; LITHOID blocks machine intelligence, not hive mind.
trait_hive_mind explicitly allows LITHOID; hive authority requires gestalt and non-MACHINE, and supplies hive trait. No native contradiction found for EEP05.

Base devouring-swarm civic accepts hive authority and this origin/civic pair; LITHOID selects its native Terravore swap. gov_devouring_swarm permits hive non-wilderness with the base civic. Do not replace base civic with display swap name.
disabled_dlcs=[] means no DLC disabled, not zero owned/active DLC. Native Lithoids/Nemesis descriptors and archives exist; host entitlement is an engine fact not proven from installed bytes alone.

EEP05 ruler.gender=not_set; playable comparator EEP02 ruler female. Official lith11 preset ruler female while species indeterminable. Native dedicated missing-ruler-gender error exists, and ruler GUI has male/female/indeterminable without species default-random button. Strong candidate, not confirmed actual failure until native error tooltip observed.

country_customization chooses colony shelters and random graphical cultures by weight, not design validation. Tiny galaxy file sets star/empire counts and geometry, no Lithoid/hive exclusion; configured language/size do not identify a design error.

ui_evidence_required: Actual EEP05 selection identity before edit, not a guessed coordinate or truncated label alone.
Unmodified editor state plus full native error tooltip in simplified Chinese; capture raw screenshot, OCR, action receipts and actual run/display identity.
Hover Save/Done before changing anything; if ruler error shown, inspect Ruler appearance page and choose-sex controls without saving.
Missing-ruler-gender text establishes that missing field; list every additional red reason, do not silently exclude.
Any future fixture change requires its own docs-first plan and a new actual selection/save verification.
